svg.title: White-Collar and Blue-Collar Industry Job Growth in the 150 Largest US Metro Areas, 2019 to 2023
svg.desc: Bubble chart. Horizontal: Finance and professional services jobs, change 2019 to 2023. Vertical: Goods-producing jobs, change 2019 to 2023. Bubble area: change in total covered jobs, 2019 to 2023; an outlined bubble is a negative value. 114 of 150 plotted; 36 not published. Austin-Round Rock-San Marcos, TX: +35.6% horizontal, +18.7% vertical, 187,324 bubble. Full data in the table below.
svg.text: Job Growth in the 150 Largest US
Industry groups standing in for white- and blue-collar work: private financial
activities and professional and business services against goods-producing
industries. Jobs are counted by employer industry, not occupation.
Finance and professional services jobs, change 2019 to 2023 →
Bubble size = change in total covered jobs, 2019 to 2023
The 150 largest metropolitan areas by 2019 total covered employment, Puerto Rico included.
Source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Quarterly Census of Employment and Wages, 2019 and 2023,
Computed by Embedding Atlas: bubble = 2023 − 2019 annual average total covered employment, all industries and
Computed by Embedding Atlas: growth = (2023 / 2019 − 1) × 100 of private annual average jobs summed over QCEW
industries 1023 + 1024 (horizontal) and 1011 + 1012 + 1013 (vertical); null if any part is withheld.
